text: When Father Hooper at last lay dying. <break time="0.8s" /> Elizabeth whose calm affection had endured in secret. <break time="0.8s" /> Through all those years. <break time="0.8s" /> Sat by his bed as his nurse. <break time="0.8s" /> The Reverend Mister Clark of Westbury. <break time="0.8s" /> A young minister. <break time="0.8s" /> Bent forward and said. <break time="0.8s" /> Before the veil of eternity is lifted. <break time="0.8s" /> Let me cast aside this black veil. <break time="0.8s" /> But Father Hooper snatched both his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> From beneath the bedclothes. <break time="0.8s" /> And pressed them strongly on the black veil. <break time="0.8s" /> Crying, Never, On earth, never. <break time="0.8s" /> Why do you tremble at me alone. <break time="0.8s" /> He cried. <break time="0.8s" /> Turning his veiled face. <break time="0.8s" /> Round the circle of pale spectators. <break time="0.8s" /> Tremble also at each other. <break time="0.8s" /> When the friend shows his inmost heart. <break time="0.8s" /> To his friend. <break time="0.8s" /> Then deem me a monster. <break time="0.8s" /> For the symbol. <break time="0.8s" /> Beneath which I have lived and die. <break time="0.8s" /> I look around me. <break time="0.8s" /> And, lo, on every visage. <break time="0.8s" /> A Black Veil. <break time="0.8s" /> He cried. <break time="0.8s" /> And his hearers shrank from one another. <break time="0.8s" /> In mutual fear. <break time="0.8s" /> Father Hooper fell back upon his pillow. <break time="0.8s" /> A veiled corpse. <break time="0.8s" /> With a faint smile on his lips. <break time="0.8s" /> And they buried him. <break time="0.8s" /> With the veil still on his face. <break time="0.8s" /> The grass of many years. <break time="0.8s" /> Has sprung up and withered. <break time="0.8s" /> On that grave. <break time="0.8s" /> And good Father Hoopers face. <break time="0.8s" /> Has long since mouldered. <break time="0.8s" /> Beneath the Black Veil.
